title: Replace Non-Coprime Numbers in Array
summary: Given an array of integers, repeatedly replace any two adjacent non-coprime numbers with their LCM until no such pairs exist.
statement: Given an array of integers, repeatedly replace any two adjacent non-coprime numbers with their LCM until no such pairs exist. The process stops when no adjacent non-coprime numbers are found. The final array, with values ≤ 10^8, is returned. Two numbers are non-coprime if their GCD is greater than 1.
constraints: Adjacent values with gcd greater than one must be replaced by their least common multiple.
A replacement may create a new non-coprime pair with the value immediately to its left.
Continue until every adjacent pair is coprime and return the unique final list.
hints: A stack exposes exactly the newest adjacency that a replacement can affect.
Push each value, then repeatedly merge the top two while their gcd exceeds one.
Replace top pair by left/gcd*right and keep checking backward.
Earlier settled adjacencies remain unchanged except the one touching the merged value, which is precisely the new stack top pair.
editorial: Earlier settled adjacencies remain unchanged except the one touching the merged value, which is precisely the new stack top pair.

tests.explanation: Cascading replacements combine the first four values to 12 and the final pair to 6, giving [12,7,6].
The two values and the trailing threes merge within their regions, producing [2,1,1,3].
